passages.text: Honeybees do more than make honey. As they move from flower to flower collecting nectar, pollen sticks to their fuzzy bodies and rubs off on the next blossom. That accidental delivery service pollinates roughly one out of every three bites of food people eat. When bee populations fall, farmers notice it in their harvests long before shoppers notice it in stores.

passages.text: For centuries, sailors navigated by the stars. A skilled navigator could fix a ship's position using only a sextant, a clock, and a clear night sky. Satellite navigation made that work almost effortless, but many naval academies still teach celestial navigation. Instruments fail, batteries die, and signals can be jammed — the stars cannot be switched off.

inference.answer: A navigator whose electronics failed could still determine the ship's position.

passages.text: Rosa Parks is often described as a tired seamstress who simply would not stand up. Her refusal on that Montgomery bus was a deliberate act by someone who understood exactly what it would set in motion.

passages.text: Each year a tree adds a new layer of wood beneath its bark, and those layers show up as rings in a cut trunk. Wide rings mean a wet, easy growing season; narrow rings mean drought or cold. Because the ring pattern is consistent across a whole region, scientists can match rings from old beams in barns to rings in living trees and date a building to a single year.

inference.answer: Two trees growing in the same region in the same years would show similar ring patterns.

passages.text: Louis Braille was blind by age five and frustrated by books with raised printed letters, which were bulky and slow to read. As a teenager he reworked a military code of raised dots into a system of six-dot cells, each standing for a letter or a number. A fingertip can feel an entire cell at once, so a reader moves down a line instead of tracing the shape of every letter.

passages.text: A sourdough starter is nothing but flour and water left out until wild yeast and bacteria move in from the air and the grain. The yeast feeds on sugars in the flour and gives off carbon dioxide, which inflates the dough into bubbles. The bacteria produce acids at the same time, and those acids give sourdough its tang. Bakers keep a starter working for years by feeding it fresh flour every few days.

inference.answer: A starter that is never fed will eventually stop working.

passages.text: Mangrove trees grow in salty water along tropical coasts, standing on tangled roots that arch above the surface. Those roots slow incoming waves and trap mud and sand, so the shoreline behind them erodes far more slowly during storms. The same tangle shelters young fish until they are big enough for open water. Coastal towns that cleared their mangroves for docks and shrimp ponds have since spent millions building seawalls to do the same job.

passages.text: Steel expands when it warms and shrinks when it cools. On a long bridge, that change can add up to several inches between a January morning and a July afternoon. Without those gaps, the deck would push against itself and buckle.
